frames.label: Scene
frames.title: Start with the room, not the instruction
frames.alt: Room view from the task-generation demonstration.
frames.caption: Objects, supporting surfaces and their geometry form the input.

frames.label: Graph
frames.title: Represent space around an anchor
frames.alt: Initial placement regions around a tabletop object.
frames.caption: A receptacle-aware graph records spatial relationships and candidate placement regions.

frames.label: Instructions
frames.title: Two ways to specify a task
frames.caption: Generate instructions grounded in the graph. The two outputs specify different things; neither is an agent rollout.

graph.title: Where can the next object fit?

frames.label: Bounds
frames.caption: Establish the platform heading and the bounding boxes of the objects it supports.

frames.label: Empty surface
frames.caption: An empty surface can be partitioned into directional regions relative to its heading.

frames.label: Anchor
frames.caption: On an occupied surface, describe possible placements relative to an anchor object.

frames.label: Extend
frames.caption: Extend bounding-box edges to the platform boundaries.

frames.label: Occupancy
frames.caption: Check which initial regions overlap existing objects.

frames.label: Cardinal
frames.caption: Refine candidate regions along the cardinal directions.

frames.label: Diagonal
frames.caption: Refine diagonal placement regions as well.

frames.label: Before merge
frames.caption: Inspect the candidate regions before merging.

frames.label: After merge
frames.caption: The merged region represents available placement space for the generator.

process.title: Compose an ordered instruction
process.note: Floral cup example · illustrations from the narrated demonstration

frames.label: Select
frames.title: Choose an object and two spatial goals
frames.caption: The example refers to a floral cup, a wooden box and two lamps in this room.

frames.label: First relation
frames.title: To the right of the box
frames.caption: The first relocation names an anchor and a direction. It constrains where the cup can be placed.

frames.label: Next relation
frames.title: Then, between the lamps
frames.caption: Compose a second relocation for the same cup. Reversing the order would describe a different task.

difficulty.title: What counts as completing a task?

frames.label: Level 1
frames.title: One relocation
frames.caption: A single relocation with a unique target. An automatic final check and intermediate points are available.

frames.label: Level 2
frames.title: Resolve ambiguity
frames.caption: The agent must distinguish relevant objects. The task is still a single relocation with automatic evaluation.

frames.label: Level 3
frames.title: Preserve the order
frames.caption: Two relocations must be completed in order. Intermediate points capture partial progress.

frames.label: Level 4
frames.title: Judge a desired outcome
frames.caption: An outcome may admit several valid arrangements. There is no intermediate score for this level.
